props.gloss_en: the verse: 'sing, barren woman who has not given birth' (Isa 54:1)
go down to the end of the verse: 'for the children of the desolate are more than the children of the married wife, said the Lord' -- the end of the verse fixes the sense of its opening
rather, what is 'barren woman who has not given birth'? -- sing, congregation of Israel, which is like a barren woman who did not bear children for Gehenna like you

objections.gloss_en: כתיב רני עקרה לא ילדה -- משום דלא ילדה, רני? -- because she has not given birth she should sing? the opening words, read plainly, are absurd

answered_by.gloss_en: שטיא, שפיל לסיפיה דקרא -- the end of the verse (כי רבים בני שוממה) shows the barren woman is Knesset Yisrael, who bore no children for Gehenna (= p_seifa_bnei_shomema, p_rani_knesset_yisrael)
